title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
spaceBreakdown:
- Trie nodes: up to N·L nodes, each with 26 pointers + 1 bool → O(N·L)
- Recursion call stack: up to L = 25 deep → O(L)
- Not counted: input strings, returned bool
approach: Use a trie (prefix tree) where each node stores 26 child pointers and an end-of-word flag. `addWord` walks from the root, creating nodes as needed and marking the final node. `search` uses DFS: for a normal letter, follow the corresponding child; for `'.'`, recursively try all non-null children. Since at most 2 dots appear per query, the branching is bounded (26² = 676), keeping search fast.
hints: When adding "bad" and "bat", which characters are identical, and how could you avoid re-examining them for each word? word.length ≤ 25 and at most 2 dots appear in any search.

Use a trie (prefix tree): each node has 26 child pointers and an end-of-word flag. Adding "bad" creates root→b→a→d with the flag set at "d"; searching ".ad" tries all children of root, then follows a→d.

```
addWord(word): walk from root, create missing nodes, set isEnd at last node
search(word): dfs(root, word, 0)
dfs(node, word, i):
    if i == len(word): return node.isEnd
    if word[i] == '.': try dfs on all non-null children, return true if any succeeds
    else: follow node.children[word[i]], return false if null
```

**Prefix not a word** - search string is a proper prefix of an added word
`Input: ["WordDictionary","addWord","search"],[[],["bad"],["ba"]]` → `Expected: [null,null,false]`
⚠️ Bug: returning true when the search index reaches the end without checking the isEnd flag → returns true

**Non-existent character** - search word has a letter not present at that trie position
`Input: ["WordDictionary","addWord","search"],[[],["bad"],["pad"]]` → `Expected: [null,null,false]`
⚠️ Bug: not checking if children[idx] is null before recursing in the non-dot branch → dereferences null pointer, crash

**Dot at last position** - wildcard is the final character, but the only matching child is not an end node
`Input: ["WordDictionary","addWord","search"],[[],["bade"],["ba."]]` → `Expected: [null,null,false]`
⚠️ Bug: when handling '.', returning true if any child exists instead of recursing to check isEnd → returns true

**Single character word** - word length is 1
`Input: ["WordDictionary","addWord","search","search"],[[],["a"],["a"],["."]]` → `Expected: [null,null,true,true]`
⚠️ Bug: using `i < word.size() - 1` as the loop bound in addWord with size_t when size is 1, making the bound 0 and skipping the only character → isEnd set on root, search("a") returns false

followUps.q: What if search also supports '*' matching zero or more of any character?
followUps.a: Extend the DFS: at '*', either skip it (match zero) or consume one character and stay at the same node (match more). This adds branching at each '*', making search O(L · 26^d · 2^s) where s is the number of '*' characters. Space stays O(N·L).

followUps.q: Add a deleteWord(word) method that removes a word from the structure.
followUps.a: Traverse to the word's end node, unset isEnd, then walk back up pruning nodes that have no children and no isEnd flag. Time O(L) per deletion, space unchanged at O(N·L).

followUps.q: Memory is tight - can you reduce per-node overhead?
followUps.a: Replace the fixed 26-pointer array with an unordered_map<char, Node*> per node. This stores only existing edges, cutting per-node overhead from 26 pointers to just the actual children. Lookup becomes O(1) amortized; big-O space stays O(N·L) but the constant factor drops dramatically for sparse tries.
